# preamble and setup

main script was getting way too long

- READING DUMP
  - https://rcompanion.org/rcompanion/d_08.html


```{r pathfinding, message=FALSE}
here::i_am("scripts/_mss/posthoc.Rmd")
```

- for NTW and CTRL comparisons, used interactive models. 
- if int was sig in either NTW or CTRL models, did simple contrasts + interaction contrast. if int was ns, used additive model and got EMMs per factor. 

## loading

```{r data and lib, message=FALSE}
library(emmeans)
library(multcomp) # for cld

source(here::here("scripts/_mss/load.R"))

# create df of just same minT group
dfs_stats <- list_modify(
  dfs_stats,
  dev_ph = dfs_stats$dev_all %>% filter(trt.minT == 26)
)
```

# # survival

## pupal

```{r}
# NTW
mods <- glmer(is.pup ~ pop*trt.minT + (1|year),
             family = "binomial", data = dfs_stats$dev_expt)

anova(mods, update(mods, . ~ . - pop:trt.minT),
      test = "Chisq") # int is sig
drop1(update(mods, . ~ . - pop:trt.minT), test = "Chisq") # both are sig

emms <- emmeans(mods, c("pop", "trt.minT"), type = "response")
emms

# pw comparisons (but also see below)
# pairs(emms, simple = "pop") 
# pairs(emms, simple = "trt.minT")
# examine pw contrasts of main effs and interaction
pairs(emms, simple = "each", combine = TRUE, infer = TRUE,
      bias.adjust = TRUE, sigma = as.numeric(VarCorr(mods))) 
contrast(emms, interaction = "pairwise", infer = TRUE, 
         bias.adjust = TRUE, sigma = as.numeric(VarCorr(mods)))
```

```{r eval=FALSE}
# understanding wtf im doing w these tests

## test if means are different
test(pairs(emms, simple = "each", combine = TRUE), type = "response", adjust = "bonferroni") 
  # tests pw contrasts, i.e. ME1 compared to e/o at the level of ME2
  # same as pairs(emms, simple = "each", combine = TRUE)
  # this is more of what we want bc we are interested in effects
test(emms, adjust = "bonferroni")# same as below
test(emms, joint = FALSE, type = "response", adjust = "bonferroni") 
  # on default settings (delta = 0), tests superiority
  # ie compare H ((estimate - null)/SE) to H0 (depends on "null" value)
  # if null = 0, tests if grps are different from e/o.
  # so rly just use this to get the estimate of the reponse
joint_tests(emms, adjust = "bonferroni") 
  # anova type III (are all effs (ME + IE) signif ≠ 0? (ignoring int))

## are means different from e/o?
summary(emms, type = "response", infer = c(TRUE))
summary(emms, type = "response", infer = c(TRUE, FALSE)) # same as test(joint = FALSE)
summary(emms, type = "response", infer = c(FALSE, TRUE))
summary(emms, type = "response", infer = c(FALSE))

## (note these are all testing if mean1 - mean2 ≠ 0, 
## not if mean1 ≠ 0(?), which is what emmeans() by itself can do)
```


```{r}
# CTRL VS EXPT
# fit
mods <- list(
  int = glmer(is.pup ~ pop*trt.type + (1|year),
             family = "binomial", data = dfs_stats$dev_ph),
  add = glmer(is.pup ~ pop + trt.type + (1|year),
             family = "binomial", data = dfs_stats$dev_ph)
)

# check main effs and int
anova(mods$add, mods$int, test = "Chisq") # int is sig
drop1(mods$add, test = "Chisq") # pop is sig

# get means and compare
emms <- emmeans(mods$int, c("pop", "trt.type"), type = "response")
emms %>% tidy() %>% write_clip()

# pairs(emms, simple = "pop") 
# pairs(emms, simple = "trt.type")
pairs(emms, simple = "each", combine = TRUE)
contrast(emms, interaction = "pairwise")

test(emms, adjust = "bonferroni")

summary(emms, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))

# cld
cld(emms, adjust = "bonferroni")
```

```{r}
# cld'ing
df <- df_stats$dev_all %>%
  mutate(trt = paste0(trt.type, "-", trt.minT))
```
## adult

```{r}
# NTW
mods <- glmer(is.ec ~ pop*trt.minT + (1|year),
             family = "binomial", data = dfs_stats$dev_expt)

drop1(mods, test = "Chisq") # int is ns
# anova(mods, update(mods, . ~ . - pop:trt.minT),
#       test = "Chisq") 
drop1(update(mods, . ~ . - pop:trt.minT), test = "Chisq") # pop is sig

# get emms separately
emms <- list(
  pop = emmeans(mods, "pop", type = "response"),
  trt = emmeans(mods, "trt.minT", type = "response"),
  int = emmeans(mods, c("pop", "trt.minT"), type = "response") 
    ## altho int is ns hard to talk abt means when effs are separated lol
  )
test(emms$pop, adjust = "bonferroni") 
test(emms$trt, adjust = "bonferroni")
test(emms$int, adjust = "bonferroni")

# test effs
pairs(emms$pop)
pairs(emms$trt)
rbind(pairs(emms$pop), pairs(emms$trt))

contrast(emms$int, interaction = "pairwise")
```

```{r}
# CTRL VS EXPT
# fit
mods <- list(
  int = glmer(is.ec ~ pop*trt.type + (1|year),
             family = "binomial", data = dfs_stats$dev_ph),
  add = glmer(is.ec ~ pop + trt.type + (1|year),
             family = "binomial", data = dfs_stats$dev_ph)
)
## both singular fits - not super surprising bc lab generally has high survival

# check main effs and int
anova(mods$add, mods$int, test = "Chisq") # int is barely sig
drop1(mods$add, test = "Chisq") # pop is sig
## int is the better model, but bc int is borderline, get EMMs on the int mod for 1 factor at a time

# get means and compare
emms <- list(
  pop = emmeans(mods$int, "pop", type = "response"),
  trt = emmeans(mods$int, "trt.type", type = "response"),
  int = emmeans(mods$int, c("pop", "trt.type"), type = "response") 
)
test(emms$pop, adjust = "bonferroni")
test(emms$trt, adjust = "bonferroni")
test(emms$int, adjust = "bonferroni")
  
pairs(emms$pop) 
pairs(emms$trt)
rbind(pairs(emms$pop), pairs(emms$trt))
```


# # mass

## pupal

```{r}
# NTW
mods <- lmer(mass.pupa ~ pop*trt.minT + sex + (1|year),
             data = dfs_stats$dev_expt %>% filter(!is.na(sex)))

anova(mods, type = 2) # all sig

emms <- list(
  int = emmeans(mods, c("pop", "trt.minT")),
  sex = emmeans(mods, "sex")
  )
test(emms$int, adjust = "bonferroni")
test(emms$sex, adjust = "bonferroni")

pairs(emms$int, simple = "pop")
pairs(emms$int, simple = "trt.minT")
pairs(emms$int, simple = "each", combine = TRUE)
pairs(emms$sex)

rbind(pairs(emms$int, simple = "each", combine = TRUE), pairs(emms$sex))

# looking at interactions..
contrast(emms$int, interaction = "pairwise")
joint_tests(mods, by = "sex") 
joint_tests(mods)

## visualise...
with_emm_options(gg.theme = ggplot2::theme_bw(),
                 emmip(mods, pop ~ trt.minT | sex, 
      CIs = TRUE, 
      ))

with_emm_options(gg.theme = ggplot2::theme_bw(),
                 emmip(mods, trt.minT ~ pop | sex, 
      CIs = TRUE, 
      ))
```

```{r}
# CTRL VS EXPT
# fit
mods <- lmer(mass.pupa ~ pop*trt.type + sex + (1|year),
             data = dfs_stats$dev_ph %>% filter(!is.na(sex)))

# check main effs and int
anova(mods, type = 2) # all are sig

# get means and compare
emms <- list(
  int = emmeans(mods, c("pop", "trt.type")),
  sex = emmeans(mods, "sex")
  )
test(emms$int, adjust = "bonferroni")
test(emms$sex, adjust = "bonferroni")

# pairs(emms$int, simple = "pop")
# pairs(emms$int, simple = "trt.type")
# pairs(emms$sex)
rbind(pairs(emms$int, simple = "each", combine = TRUE), pairs(emms$sex)) %>% tidy() %>% write_clip()
contrast(emms$int, interaction = "pairwise")
```

# # lifespan

## 2023
```{r}
# NTW
mods <- lm(tt.long ~ pop*trt.minT,
           data = dfs_stats$dev_expt %>% filter(year == 2023, 
                                                if.mated == 1, if.fridge == 0))

drop1(mods, test = "F") # int is ns, so use the additive
mods <- update(mods, ~ . - pop:trt.minT)

drop1(mods, test = "F") # everything ns

emms <- list(
  pop = emmeans(mods, "pop"),
  trt = emmeans(mods, "trt.minT")
  )
test(emms$pop, adjust = "bonferroni") %>% tidy() %>% write_clip()
test(emms$trt, adjust = "bonferroni") %>% tidy() %>% write_clip()

pairs(emms$pop)
pairs(emms$trt)
rbind(pairs(emms$pop), pairs(emms$trt))
```

```{r}
# CTRL
mods <- lm(tt.long ~ pop*trt.type,
           data = dfs_stats$dev_ph %>% filter(year == 2023, 
                                              if.mated == 1, if.fridge == 0))

drop1(mods, test = "F") # int is ns

mods <- update(mods, ~ . - pop:trt.type)
drop1(mods, test = "F") # pop is sig

emms <- list(
  pop = emmeans(mods, "pop"),
  trt = emmeans(mods, "trt.type")
  )
test(emms$pop, adjust = "bonferroni") %>% tidy() %>% write_clip()
test(emms$trt, adjust = "bonferroni") %>% tidy() %>% write_clip()

pairs(emms$pop)
pairs(emms$trt)
rbind(pairs(emms$pop), pairs(emms$trt)) 
```

# # eggs laid

## 2023
```{r}
df <- dfs_stats$eggs %>%
  filter(year == 2023)
```


```{r}
# (fit mods separately for w/in and btwn..?)

# trying to do all trts tgt
mods <- list(
  all = glmer(n.coll ~ trt.minT + mate.ishs + (1|cage), offset = log(n.f),
              family = "poisson", data = df),
  all2 = glmer(n.coll ~ trt.type + trt.minT + mate.istrt + (1|cage), offset = log(n.f),
               family = "poisson", data = df)
)

drop1(mods$all, test = "Chisq") # all ns
drop1(mods$all2, test = "Chisq") # all ns

emms <- list(
  all = emmeans(mods$all, ~ .),
  all2 = emmeans(mods$all2, ~ .)
) 

emms$all
emms$all %>% rbind() # this makes more sense...
emms$all2 %>% rbind()

pairs(emms$all, infer = TRUE)
pairs(emms$all2, infer = TRUE)
```
